input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 runs in the wrong direction: it imposes on Customer an open-ended obligation to disclose and match, for Vendor's benefit, any more favourable commercial offer it receives, with no defined product, no time limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs. That is walk-away territory under MFN and fails every fallback element, so we cured it at the preferred level by removing the Customer-side obligation. It also contradicts Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment, which our edit conforms. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing in our favour is affected.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to disclose to, or match for, Vendor any commercial offer it receives from another provider.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed Section 7.2's open-ended obligation to disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit, since our playbook does not accept an MFN running against us; Section 12.3 already confirms we make no most-favoured-customer commitment. If Vendor needs something, we could consider an MFN limited to one defined product for 12 months with like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
proposal.summary: Turn Section 7.2's Customer disclose-and-match MFN obligation into an express statement that no such obligation exists.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
